core_obligations: Statement (lines 1672-1680): if f is representable, there is a formula A_f with Q proving A_f(numerals, num m) iff m = f(numerals).
The 'if' direction is clause rep:a of the representability definition (stated in-span by the author).

The 'only if' direction (proof lines 1682-1704): assume Q proves A_f at num m with m != f; let l = f(numerals); rep:a gives provability at num l; rep:b gives the uniqueness universal; logic yields Q proves num l = num m; the inequation stub gives the negation - Q inconsistent, contradicting satisfiability of Q by the standard model and soundness.
proof_roadmap: Identify the 'if' direction with definition clause rep:a.
Run the 'only if' uniqueness contradiction from rep:a and rep:b.
Close with numeral inequation plus consistency of Q.
